title: The bow, the arrow, the target — om is the bow, the self the arrow, Brahman the mark (2.2)
hook: the Mundaka turns meditation into archery: om is the bow, the self is the arrow, Brahman is the target
carry: like the arrow, become one with it
tomorrow: the two birds on one tree

segments.voice: Yesterday: visphulinga, sparks of the same form, flying from one blazing fire and returning to it. Your line was sparks.

Watch an archer just before the release. The whole body goes still. The breath slows, then stops. The eyes stop darting. For one second there's nothing in the world but the line from the arrowhead to the mark. Let the mind drift to dinner, and the arrow drifts with it. So when the Mundaka wants to describe meditation, it doesn't reach for a cushion or a mountain cave. It hands you a bow.
screen: `THE MOMENT BEFORE THE RELEASE.` → `THINK OF DINNER, AND YOU MISS.` → `THE MUNDAKA HANDS YOU A BOW.`

segments.voice: Two verses do it. The first: take the great weapon of the Upanishad as your bow. Fit to it an arrow sharpened by meditation. Draw it back with a mind absorbed in that, and hit the target, dear one: the imperishable. Then the second verse spells out the picture. Pranavo dhanuh: om is the bow. Sharo hy atma: the self is the arrow. Brahma tal lakshyam uchyate: Brahman is called the target. Then two instructions. It must be struck by one who isn't careless, apramatta, undistracted. And then: sharavat tanmayo bhavet. Like the arrow, become one with it. When an arrow hits its mark, it doesn't stay separate, hovering an inch away. It goes in. It becomes part of the target. Tanmaya means made of that, full of that, absorbed in it. You met that -maya, made of, a few weeks ago in the Taittiriya: the self made of food, of breath, of mind. Now the text asks you to become tan-maya, made of that. Why is om the bow? Teachers explain that the sound, chanted or held in the mind, gathers attention and sends it. The next verse adds: know the one self alone, in which sky and earth and mind are woven. Let go of other talk. This is the bridge to the deathless. And then a blessing: may you cross safely to the far shore, beyond darkness.
screen: `THE UPANISHAD IS THE BOW.` · `OM THE BOW, THE SELF THE ARROW.` · `BRAHMAN THE TARGET.` · `LIKE THE ARROW, BECOME ONE WITH IT.` · then, large: `TANMAYA.`

segments.voice: Sit tall, like a drawn bow, and let a soft om come out on the breath, or simply hear it inside, gathering your attention the way a bow gathers its pull. Let the attention fly to one point, the stillness after the sound. When the mind wanders, and it will, notice it without blame, and draw the bow again.
The bow. In the Mundaka, om is the bow, the self is the arrow, Brahman is the target, and the archer becomes one with it, like the arrow in the mark.
Your line: like the arrow, become one with it. Tomorrow, two birds on one tree. Day four hundred sixteen.

howItsDone: Hindus who meditate with om chant it aloud or hold it in the mind, and some teachers use the Mundaka's bow and arrow to describe how the sound gathers attention toward one point.
